MOUNTAIN VIEW REGIONAL EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT
Patient: TESTPATIENT, ALEX   DOB: 01/01/1980   MRN: 000111
Arrival: 03/14/2024 18:42  Mode: private vehicle
Chief complaint: neck pain after motor vehicle collision
HPI: 44 y/o restrained driver, rear-ended at a stoplight approx 1 hr prior. Reports posterior neck pain 6/10, denies LOC, denies numbness or tingling.
Exam: Paraspinal tenderness C4-C6. No midline tenderness. Strength 5/5 bilateral upper extremities.
Assessment: Cervical strain.
Disposition: Discharged home with ibuprofen. Follow up with PCP in 1 week.

label: office_visit
text:
FAMILY MEDICINE ASSOCIATES - PROGRESS NOTE
Date of service: 03/21/2024
Subjective: Follow up for neck pain since MVC on 03/14/2024. Pain improved from 6/10 to 4/10. Some stiffness in the mornings. Sleeping better.
Objective: Decreased cervical rotation to the right. No neurological deficits.
Assessment/Plan: 1. Cervical strain, improving. Refer to physical therapy 2x/week for 6 weeks. Continue NSAIDs as needed. Return in 4 weeks.

label: office_visit
text:
ORTHOPEDIC CONSULTATION
Referring provider: Dr. Sample
History: Right shoulder pain for 3 months. Patient reports a prior shoulder injury playing softball in 2019, resolved without treatment.
Exam: Positive Neer and Hawkins on the right. Full passive range of motion.
Impression: Right shoulder impingement, rule out rotator cuff tear.
Plan: MRI right shoulder without contrast. Subacromial injection offered, patient will consider.

label: therapy_note
text:
PHYSICAL THERAPY DAILY NOTE  Visit 4 of 12
Dx: Cervical strain (S16.1XXA)
Patient reports 3/10 neck pain today, able to drive 30 minutes without increase in symptoms.
Treatment: Manual therapy 15 min, therapeutic exercise 20 min (chin tucks, scapular retraction, thoracic extension), moist heat 10 min.
Assessment: Improving cervical ROM, rotation now 60 deg bilaterally.
Plan: Continue per plan of care. Progress to resisted rows next visit.

label: therapy_note
text:
CHIROPRACTIC TREATMENT RECORD
Date: 04/02/2024
Subjective: Lower back tight, 5/10, worse after sitting.
Segments adjusted: L4, L5, SI joint right.
Modalities: electrical stimulation 12 minutes, intersegmental traction.
Response to treatment: patient tolerated well, reports decreased tightness post adjustment.
Next visit: 04/05/2024

label: imaging_report
text:
RADIOLOGY REPORT
Exam: XR CERVICAL SPINE 3 VIEWS
Clinical indication: neck pain after MVC
Comparison: None.
Findings: Normal alignment. Vertebral body heights are maintained. Mild disc space narrowing at C5-C6 with small anterior osteophytes. No acute fracture. Prevertebral soft tissues within normal limits.
Impression: No acute fracture. Mild degenerative changes at C5-C6.
Electronically signed by: R. Example, MD

label: imaging_report
text:
MRI RIGHT SHOULDER WITHOUT CONTRAST
Technique: Multiplanar multisequence MR imaging of the right shoulder.
Findings: Partial thickness articular surface tear of the supraspinatus tendon measuring 6 mm. Mild subacromial-subdeltoid bursitis. Type II acromion. Labrum intact.
IMPRESSION:
1. Partial thickness supraspinatus tear.
2. Mild bursitis.

label: procedure_report
text:
PROCEDURE NOTE
Procedure: Right subacromial corticosteroid injection under ultrasound guidance
Indication: Right shoulder impingement
Consent: Risks including infection, bleeding and tendon weakening discussed; written consent obtained.
Technique: Skin prepped with chlorhexidine. 25-gauge needle advanced into the subacromial space under direct visualization. Injected 40 mg triamcinolone with 4 mL 1% lidocaine.
Complications: None. Patient tolerated the procedure well.

label: procedure_report
text:
OPERATIVE REPORT
Preoperative diagnosis: Right shoulder rotator cuff tear
Postoperative diagnosis: Same
Procedure: Arthroscopic rotator cuff repair, subacromial decompression
Anesthesia: General with interscalene block
Estimated blood loss: minimal
Findings: Full thickness tear of the supraspinatus, 1.5 cm. Repaired with two suture anchors.
The patient was taken to recovery in stable condition.

label: education_handout
text:
PATIENT EDUCATION: HOME EXERCISES FOR NECK PAIN
1. Chin tucks: sit tall, gently draw your chin straight back. Hold 5 seconds. Repeat 10 times.
2. Shoulder rolls: roll shoulders backward in a slow circle 10 times.
Stop any exercise that causes sharp pain and contact your provider.
